name: TX-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+11 partisan lean strongly favors incumbent Keith Self
Prediction markets price Self near 94% to win reelection
Hunt's $649K raised shows a real effort but he trails badly in cash on hand
No public general-election polling, keeping uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean, Self's incumbency and cash advantage, and market pricing near 94% Republican all point to a Self win; Hunt's solid fundraising keeps the race out of safe territory but falls short of a genuine threat.
model.watch: Fresh polling, a surge of outside spending behind Hunt, or a sharply favorable national environment for Democrats could move the race toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District, anchored in Collin County north of Dallas, leans Republican by about eleven points, and Representative Keith Self is seeking reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. No public general-election polling is available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, candidate finances, and betting markets. Prediction markets give Self roughly a 94% chance of winning, placing the seat firmly in Republican hands.

Democrat Evan Hunt has run a serious fundraising effort, bringing in about $649,000, but he ends the period with far less cash on hand than Self, who holds a financial edge and has drawn modest outside support. Hunt's haul shows the campaign is active, yet nothing in the record indicates the district's partisan balance has shifted enough to put the incumbent in danger. The race is best characterized as likely Republican, with an upset requiring an unusually strong national environment.
